newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bidding interest in Creditanstalt seems tepid.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bidding interest in Creditanstalt seems tepid.

text.p: If any U.S. banks are interested in acquiring a 70 percent stake in Austrian bank Creditanstalt-Bankverein through a government privitization, they are keeping a low profile for now.

Although names of several big U.S. players have circulated through the rumor mill, including Citicorp and BankAmerica Corp, sources close to the situation said Tuesday those two banks could be scratched off the list of potential buyers.

Buying a stake in Creditanstalt does not seem to fit with Citicorp's strategy of building a corporate banking business and then a consumer business in fast-growing emerging markets, the sources said. BankAmerica is still wrestling with what strategies it wants to pursue in Europe and Japan and an announcement could be a month or two away.

On Monday, Morgan Stanley & Co analyst Arthur Soter said BankAmerica was likely to focus on businesses in Europe and Japan that it finds most profitable and get out of some lies. A complete withdrawal from Europe by BankAmerica is considered very unlikely.
At the same time, according to the sources, a purchase of Creditanstalt stake by BankAmerica is not in the cards.
A BankAmerica spokesman would only say that the bank has a policy of no comment on speculation about what it might or might not do in the fiture.
A Citicorp spokesman said the company does not respond to rumors.
A spokesman for another rumored buyer, General Electric Co's GE Capital, was not immediately available for comment.
An Austrian banker based in New York said just that the process of finding bidders has been going on for a long time and he has not heard anything new.
